arxiv-2012-03107.title: When Do Curricula Work?
arxiv-2012-03107.creator: Xiaoxia Wu, Ethan Dyer, Behnam Neyshabur
arxiv-2012-03107.description: Abstract Inspired by human learning, researchers have proposed ordering examples during training based on their difficulty. Both curriculum learning, exposing a network to easier examples early in training, and anti-curriculum learning, showing the most difficult examples first, have been suggested as improvements to the standard i.i.d. training.

arxiv-2111-09419.title: Determination of complete experiments using graphs
arxiv-2111-09419.creator: Y. Wunderlich, P. Kroenert, F. Afzal and A. Thiel
arxiv-2111-09419.description: Abstract This work presents ideas for the determination of complete experiments using graphs, which are based on a recently published, modified form of Moravcsik’s theorem. The lucid representation of complete experiments in terms of graphs, which is at the heart of the theorem, leads to a fully automated procedure that can determine complete experiments for in principle any reaction, i.e.

arxiv-2202-10212.title: Optimal Feedback Controls of Stochastic Linear Quadratic Control Problems in Infinite Dimensions with Random Coefficients
arxiv-2202-10212.creator: Qi Lü, Tianxiao Wang
arxiv-2202-10212.description: Abstract It is a longstanding unsolved problem to characterize the optimal feedback controls for general linear quadratic optimal control problem of stochastic evolution equation with random coefficients. A solution to this problem is given in [ 21 ] under some assumptions which can be verified for interesting concrete models, such as controlled stochastic wave equations, controlled stochastic Schrödinger equations, etc.

arxiv-2208-12872.title: Accelerating Tests of General Relativity with Gravitational-Wave Signals using Hybrid Sampling
arxiv-2208-12872.creator: Noah E. Wolfe, Colm Talbot, Jacob Golomb
arxiv-2208-12872.description: Abstract The Advanced LIGO/Virgo interferometers have observed ∼ 100 \sim 100 gravitational-wave transients enabling new questions to be answered about relativity, astrophysics, and cosmology. However, many of our current procedures for computing these constraints will not scale well with the increased size of future transient catalogs.

arxiv-2302-05732.title: Entanglement in the Quantum Spherical Model - a Review
arxiv-2302-05732.creator: Sascha Wald, Raul Arias, Vincenzo Alba
arxiv-2302-05732.description: Abstract We review some recent results on entanglement in the Quantum Spherical Model (QSM). The focus lays on the physical results rather than the mathematical details. Specifically, we study several entanglement-related quantities, such as entanglement entropies, and logarithmic negativity, in the presence of quantum and classical critical points, and in magnetically ordered phases.

arxiv-2310-09997.title: Forecaster: Towards Temporally Abstract Tree-Search Planning from Pixels
arxiv-2310-09997.creator: Thomas JiralerspongMcGill University, MilaMontreal, Canada thomas.jiralerspong@mail.mcgill.ca, Flemming KondrupMcGill University, MilaMontreal, Canada flemming.kondrup@mail.mcgill.ca Doina PrecupMcGill University, MilaMontreal, Canada dprecup@cs.mcgill.ca Khimya KhetarpalMila khetarpk@mila.quebec
arxiv-2310-09997.description: Abstract The ability to plan at many different levels of abstraction enables agents to envision the long-term repercussions of their decisions and thus enables sample-efficient learning. This becomes particularly beneficial in complex environments from high-dimensional state space such as pixels, where the goal is distant and the reward sparse.

arxiv-2311-13029.title: Systematic word meta-sense extension
arxiv-2311-13029.creator: Lei Yu
arxiv-2311-13029.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lei Yu. The meaning of polysemous words often varies in a highly productive yet predictable way. Generalizing the regularity between conventional senses to derive novel word meaning is crucial for automated processing of non-literal language uses such as figurative expressions. We introduce a novel task called s ystematic wo rd m eta-sense e xtension (SWORME) to test and improve language models’ ability to extend word meaning to denote new semantic domains (also called meta-senses) that bear regular semantic relations with existing senses.

arxiv-2411-07302.title: Merit-Based Sortition in Decentralized Systems
arxiv-2411-07302.creator: Kruijssen et al
arxiv-2411-07302.description: Abstract In decentralized systems, it is often necessary to select an ‘active’ subset of participants from the total participant pool, with the goal of satisfying computational limitations or optimizing resource efficiency. This selection can sometimes be made at random, mirroring the sortition practice invented in classical antiquity aimed at achieving a high degree of statistical representativeness.

arxiv-2503-18720.title: On a mixed problem for the nonstationary Stokes system in an angle
arxiv-2503-18720.creator: Jürgen Rossmann
arxiv-2503-18720.description: Abstract 1 Introduction Let K be an angle with aperture \alpha , K=\{x=(x_{1},x_{2}):\ 0<r<\infty,\ 0<\varphi<\alpha\} , where r , \varphi denote the polar coordinates of the point x . The sides of K are the half-lines \Gamma_{1} and \Gamma_{2} , where \varphi=0 on \Gamma_{1} and \varphi=\alpha on \Gamma_{2} .

arxiv-2503-22839.title: The Universe is Odd
arxiv-2503-22839.creator: Shiyin Shen (沈世银), Nan Li (李楠)
arxiv-2503-22839.description: Abstract The cosmological principle posits that the universe does not exhibit any specific preference for position or direction. However, it remains unclear whether the universe has a distinct preference for parity—whether certain properties are more likely to be classified as even or odd.

europmc-pmc8035082.title: The glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) regulates body weight and food intake via CNS-GIPR signaling.
europmc-pmc8035082.creator: Zhang Q, Delessa CT, Augustin R, Bakhti M, Colldén G, Drucker DJ, Feuchtinger A, Caceres CG, Grandl G, Harger A, Herzig S, Hofmann S, Holleman CL, Jastroch M, Keipert S, Kleinert M, Knerr PJ, Kulaj K, Legutko B, Lickert H, Liu X, Luippold G, Lutter D, Malogajski E, Medina MT, Mowery SA, Blutke A, Perez-Tilve D, Salinno C, Sehrer L, DiMarchi RD, Tschöp MH, Stemmer K, Finan B, Wolfrum C, Müller TD.

pmc-10573986.title: Comparative Study of Male and Female Patients Undergoing Frozen Elephant Trunk Total Arch Replacement
pmc-10573986.creator: Julia Benk, Tim Berger, Stoyan Kondov, Matthias D’Inka, Magdalena Bork, Tim Walter, Philipp Discher, Bartosz Rylski, Martin Czerny, Maximilian Kreibich, Reinhard Kopp
pmc-10573986.description: Background: Our aim was to investigate outcomes and long-term survival in male and female patients after frozen elephant trunk (FET) total arch replacement. Methods: Between March 2013 and January 2023, 362 patients underwent aortic arch replacement via the FET technique. We compared patient characteristics and intra- and postoperative data between male and female patients.

pmc-12519944.title: Global anaesthesia practice using inguinal hernia surgery as a tracer condition: a secondary analysis of an international prospective cohort study
pmc-12519944.creator: Cortland Linder, Cortland Linder, Maria Picciochi, Sakina Bhaloo, Ebenezer Amofa, Canada Gaston, Jose Andres Calvache, Sivesh Kamarajah, Palesa Motshabi, Dmitri Nepogodiev, Dhruv Ghosh, Laura Kudrna, Maame Jenny, Muyiwa Rotimi, Telesphore Kabera, Virginia Ledda, Sam Lawday, Craig McClain, Cliff Shel
pmc-12519944.description: SummaryIntroductionRestoration of surgical capacity is essential to post‐COVID‐19 recovery. This study explored the use and safety of anaesthesia options for inguinal hernia surgery, a common tracer condition, to describe current global practice and highlight opportunities to build the capacity of health systems.

pmc-12524816.title: Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy and Biomarkers: A Promising Perspective?
pmc-12524816.creator: Federico Barocelli, Nicolò Pasini, Alberto Bettella, Antonio Crocamo, Enrico Ambrosini, Filippo Luca Gurgoglione, Eleonora Canu, Laura Torlai Triglia, Francesca Russo, Angela Guidorossi, Francesca Maria Notarangelo, Domenico Corradi, Antonio Percesepe, Giampaolo Niccoli, Luisa Mestroni, Gjin Ndrepep
pmc-12524816.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM; MIM #107970) is a primitive heart muscle disease characterized by progressive myocardial loss and fibrosis or fibrofatty replacement, predisposing patients to ventricular arrhythmias, sudden cardiac death, and heart failure. Despite advances in imaging and genetics, early diagnosis remains challenging due to incomplete penetrance, variable phenotypic expressivity, and the fact that fatal arrhythmic events may often occur in the early stages of the disease.

pmc-12644679.title: Evaluating cell AI foundation models in kidney pathology with human-in-the-loop enrichment
pmc-12644679.creator: Junlin Guo, Siqi Lu, Can Cui, Ruining Deng, Tianyuan Yao, Zhewen Tao, Yizhe Lin, Marilyn Lionts, Quan Liu, Juming Xiong, Yu Wang, Shilin Zhao, Catie Chang, Mitchell Wilkes, Agnes Fogo, Mengmeng Yin, Haichun Yang, Yuankai Huo
pmc-12644679.description: BackgroundLarge-scale artificial intelligence foundation models have emerged as promising tools for addressing healthcare challenges, including digital pathology. While many have been developed for complex tasks such as disease diagnosis and tissue quantification using extensive and diverse datasets, their readiness for seemingly simpler tasks, such as nuclei segmentation within a single organ (for example, the kidney), remains unclear.

pmc-12651743.title: Individualized Triplet Chemotherapy Decision-Making in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: A Machine-Learning-Driven Study †
pmc-12651743.creator: Mehmet Kayaalp, Erman Akkuş, Beliz Bahar Karaoğlan, Güngör Utkan, Mohamed Shehata
pmc-12651743.description: Simple SummaryManaging metastatic colorectal cancer is challenging, and although intensive chemotherapy regimens such as FOLFOXIRI or FOLFIRINOX can provide substantial benefit, they are not appropriate for every patient. This study aimed to develop a tool that helps clinicians identify which individuals are most likely to benefit from these intensive treatments.

pmc-12965824.title: A Predictive Model for Moderate or Severe Neonatal Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome in Extremely Preterm Infants with Premature Rupture of Membranes: Development and Internal Validation
pmc-12965824.creator: Yuan Hu, Qin Li, Xiaolin Wen, Changyong Wan, Yu Lang, Sheng Chen, Ling Yan
pmc-12965824.description: PurposePreterm premature rupture of membranes (PROM) is a major cause of extremely preterm birth. Intrauterine infection and inflammation markedly increase the risk of neonatal acute respiratory distress syndrome (NARDS), particularly moderate or severe cases associated with poor outcomes. This study developed and validated a prediction model for moderate or severe NARDS in this population using inflammatory biomarkers.

pmc-13196478.title: Transdiagnostic divergent neural development of reward anticipation in early adolescents at risk for depression and psychosis
pmc-13196478.creator: Yating Huang, Hui Xu, Wanling Zhang, Jingwen Jin, Ying Li, Chao Yan
pmc-13196478.description: BackgroundReward anticipation is a transdiagnostic factor relevant to both depression and psychosis. Adolescence is a critical neurodevelopmental period when these reward-related circuits—including frontostriatal, limbic/insular, and striatal circuits may contribute to shared vulnerability across disorders, yet longitudinal transdiagnostic comparisons in early adolescents remain scarce.

pmc-13331299.title: Deficiencies in Faculty Educator Development: A Survey Perspective from the Emergency Department
pmc-13331299.creator: Sharon Lai Ching Chong, Yuan Helen Zhang, Eunizar Binte Omar, Fatimah Lateef
pmc-13331299.description: Introduction:Faculty development is crucial to sustaining medical education excellence, yet structured, targeted approaches remain limited in emergency medicine. This study explores emergency physicians’ perceptions of their educator roles and identifies faculty development needs in Singapore.Methods:A cross-sectional electronic survey was conducted from March to June 2024 across three emergency departments.

pmc-13468102.creator: Yujie Wu, Zhiwei Zhang, Wenjuan Guo, Fulin Chen, Yanghui Fang, Shubin Li, Liang Fang, Linfeng Li

pmc-13633953.title: Rates of maximal blood lactate accumulation in the extreme intensity exercise domain: implications for training prescription
pmc-13633953.creator: Ozgur Ozkaya, Hakan As, Arda Peker, Mark Burnley, Andrew M. Jones
pmc-13633953.description: PurposeThis study investigated the rate of blood lactate accumulation (vLa) across six maximal sprint efforts and identified a breakpoint (vLaBP) in the vLa–power relationship.MethodsTwelve physically active males completed 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30-s all-out sprints in randomised order on separate days, with resistances set at 10 to 12.5% of body mass.

pmc-13668184.title: Choroidal vascularity index changes in proliferative and nonproliferative macular telangiectasia type 2
pmc-13668184.creator: Zeynep Eylul Ercan, Gulsah Gokgoz, İmren Akkoyun, Gursel Yilmaz
pmc-13668184.description: PURPOSE:This study aimed to evaluate the choroidal vascularity index (CVI) in patients with nonproliferative and proliferative macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel-2) compared to healthy controls, assess the impact of ellipsoid zone (EZ) disruption on CVI, and determine whether CVI measurements vary with different binarization areas.MATERIALS AND METHODS:CVIs from MacTel-2 eyes were compared to those of healthy controls.

pmc-13677571.title: Image-Guided Decubitus Craniospinal Irradiation Setup in a Fixed-Beam Proton Room: Accuracy and Efficiency
pmc-13677571.creator: Qi Zeng, Zhiqiang Han, Arpit Chhabra, Huifang Zhai, Qing Chen, Andy Shim, Andrew Okhuereigbe, Anh Kha, Jewel Graham, Anya Burke, Meng Wei Ho, Francis Yu, Yao Yu, Yoshiya Yamada, Charles B. Simone, Haibo Lin, Dong Han
pmc-13677571.description: PurposeRecent developments have further demonstrated the feasibility of craniospinal irradiation (CSI) delivery using simplified beam arrangements, such as a single posterior brain beam. Extending these advances, CSI delivered in the lateral decubitus position within a fixed-beam proton room offers an opportunity to improve room utilization and treatment access but introduces unique challenges in patient setup and image guidance.

uslaw-usc-t11-s744.title: 11 U.S.C. § 744 — Executory contracts
uslaw-usc-t11-s744.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t11-s744.description: United States Code, Title 11 (Bankruptcy); Chapter 7 (Liquidation); Subchapter III (Stockbroker Liquidation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Notwithstanding section 365(d)(1) of this title, the trustee shall assume or reject, under section 365 of this title, any executory contract of the debtor for the purchase or sale of a security in the ordinary course of the debtor’s business, within a reasonable time.
